about: The user's own AFM sample library, with the values they measured and certified. These are ACCEPTANCE TESTS: numbers the software must reproduce, not training data. Source: 'SAMPLE CATALOG Layout2.docx', AFM Sample DATABASE, Matteo Lorenzoni (IIT), read 2026-09-02.
note_on_channels: Several entries were measured on non-height channels (KPFM potential, Young modulus, current, phase). Only the height-channel numbers are usable as tests today; the others are recorded so the value is not lost when other channels are added.
caveat: The catalog carries exported figures, not raw files. To run these as automated tests the raw scans are needed -- expected in the 13 GB batch.

samples.name: HOPG
samples.probe: SCM-PIT Bruker, k~2.8 N/m, f0~75 kHz
samples.morphology: atomically flat terraces separated by steps

samples.name: Teflon
samples.morphology: drawn polymer, elongated bands along the draw direction

height_test.why: the flatness floor of the whole library. If the pipeline cannot return 36 pm here, its levelling is adding roughness rather than removing it.

samples.name: Anodic porous alumina
samples.measured_how: pore radius by masking + grain analysis in Gwyddion; pitch from the 2D FFT of the phase image

height_test.why: the one sample that tests BOTH broken measurements at once: the object counter must find features that go DOWN, and the periodicity must return 74 nm rather than the two-pixel limit.

samples.name: Gold electrodes
samples.morphology: patterned electrode with straight edges, ~200 nm tall

height_test.why: a lithographic step with straight edges: the clean case for the ISO middle-third step measurement, and a stand-in for the film-thickness scratches.
periodic but NOT straight: the pattern meanders, so a direction-averaged method must still find the spacing.

samples.name: PMMA film
samples.calibration: tip calibrated on the Asylum PS/LDPE standard, PS reference 2 GPa

samples.name: TiO2 nanorods in PMMA
samples.morphology: nanorod aggregates embedded in a PMMA matrix

height_test.why: 3-4 nm wide against a ~25 nm tip radius: the apparent width will be many times the real one. The pipeline must NOT report the measured width as the object's.

samples.name: Lambda DNA on mica
samples.morphology: single filaments crossing a flat mica background
samples.measured_how: tip deconvolution done by hand in the catalog: apparent width 2x = 4*sqrt(R_tip*R_feature), so R_feature = (2x)^2 / (16*R_tip)

height_test.why: the worked example of the tip correction, with the user's own numbers. A filament 1.34 nm tall reads 40 nm wide and is really about 10 nm.

samples.name: DVD
samples.morphology: spiral track with elongated pits along it

height_test.why: THE periodicity test. A certified pitch, already reproduced to within 0.9% by a plain FFT. The pool contains our own DVD scan, on which the current periodicity measurement returns a 22 nm period -- the two-pixel limit -- instead of the track spacing.
